text:
[curious] Quick quiz. What does quitting Adobe cost?
A... nothing. B... one click. C... HALF the rest of your year.
[pause] On the "annual, paid monthly" plan... it was C.
Honestly, I'd stop reading at "monthly."
Take it literally, though. ANNUAL. A one-year promise.
Quit inside that year, and you owe half the payments left.
That's an early termination fee... a charge for leaving early.
[pause] For you, that means: quit after month three, still owe four and a half months.
The FTC, America's consumer watchdog, says that fee was buried in fine print or tiny hover icons.
[playful] Buried. No shovel needed. Just a magnifying glass.
Gut check: do you know YOUR cancel fees?
[pause] Why does one fee matter? Follow the money.
Subscriptions were ELEVEN percent of Adobe's revenue in twenty eleven... about ninety-six by twenty twenty-five.
[pause] For you, that means your monthly payment isn't a side hustle. It IS the business.
In twenty twenty-four, the Justice Department sued, calling canceling an "obstacle course."
[playful] No actual hurdles. Just menus... and, the FTC says, reps who stall.
In twenty twenty-six, Adobe settled: seventy-five million in civil penalties, no admission of wrongdoing.
[pause]
[surprised] The part that got me? The fee itself... is NOT banned.
Adobe just has to show it, math included, before you subscribe.
[serious] BREAKING: price tag... now located ON the product.
For you, that means the fee stays. It just can't hide.
Next time, before you hit subscribe, search the page for "commitment."
Then comment the sneakiest cancel fee you've found. Sources are pinned.
